items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The Howard was like a variety theater... So that’s where I used to go

ctx.x: So the distinction was sort of – the Dunbar was where the – let’s say the shorties went, and the Howard was for the adults, more or less.

Well, the Dunbar was – the Howard was like a variety theater. You could go there and see shows. They didn’t really show that many good pictures there. Their thing was basically for the shows. They’d have something to stick in there between shows, but it wasn’t like big-time theater. Up on U Street was where the theaters – where you could see the best movies. So that’s where I used to go, because you couldn’t go downtown

anywhere. You could, but you had to sit way upstairs in the crow’s nest in the balcony. I really wasn’t there for that one. So we had three theaters that we could go to – four – five, actually, if you’re going to count Dunbar and Howard.

items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: Jimmy and Percy and Milt Jackson and Jeff Davis and Joe Harris, the drummer -- and myself.

ctx.x: And Jimmy was playing alto then.
Yeah, Jimmy was playing the alto. We did a few dates out in California when we did that Savoy thing that they call "Maggie..." You've seen that one; that two-album thing.
